**2B.8 Research Note: Vladimir Putin in 2024**

Bottom line: the year’s record is **mostly against** crisis de-escalation and accidental-war prevention. The only pro-side evidence is narrow: one public disclaimer about a nuclear exercise and one procedural discipline decree. Against that, Putin repeatedly used deterrence drills, doctrine revision, and readiness signaling tied to the Ukraine war.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Slightly for 2B.8 | `Указ Президента Российской Федерации от 01.03.2024 г. № 162` | Kremlin | 2024-03-01 | https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/50378/print | Putin amended military statutes to require commanders to prevent crimes and incidents, report problems promptly, respond to weapons-storage alarms, and define actions for nuclear, chemical, and biological attack scenarios. This is the clearest 2024 procedural-safety evidence, but it is indirect rather than a public crisis-de-escalation move. | 2B.8, 1B.3, 1B.7 |
| Slightly for 2B.8 | `Answers by Vladimir Putin and Alexander Lukashenko to media questions` | President of Russia | 2024-05-09 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/transcripts/74002 | Putin said a tactical nuclear drill was “not about using these weapons” and “just routine work.” This is the closest de-escalatory phrasing I found in 2024, but it was limited to a live nuclear exercise in Belarus. | 2B.8, 1B.1, 1B.2 |
| Against 2B.8 | `Russia to practice tactical nuclear weapon scenario to deter West` | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-05-06 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-to-practice-tactical-nuclear-weapon-scenario-to-deter-west--defence-ministry-3419973 | Russia announced tactical nuclear drills framed as deterrence against the West. That is signaling meant to stiffen resolve and intimidate, not to reduce accidental war risk. | 2B.8, 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.5 |
| Against 2B.8 | `Russia begins second stage of tactical nuclear weapon drills with Belarus` | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-06-11 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-begins-second-stage-of-tactical-nuclear-weapon-drills-with-belarus-3478894 | The Belarus drill phase expanded readiness and cross-border operationalization. It shows continued escalation practice, not preservation of deconfliction channels. | 2B.8, 1B.1, 1B.5 |
| Against 2B.8 | `Russia will change nuclear doctrine because of Western role in Ukraine` | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-09-01 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-will-change-nuclear-doctrine-due-to-wests-actions-in-ukraine-official-says-3596699 | Moscow justified the doctrine revision as a response to Western involvement in Ukraine. That is classic coercive crisis signaling, not careful de-escalation. | 2B.8, 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.4 |
| Against 2B.8 | `Expanded meeting of the Ministry of Defence board` | President of Russia | 2024-12-16 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/75887 | Putin said Russia had specified nuclear-use principles, kept non-strategic nuclear forces on constant alert, and continued exercises while linking posture to U.S. missile deployments. That is sustained escalatory messaging rather than a crisis off-ramp. | 2B.8, 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.3 |

**Synthesis**

- Best-supported answer: **No**.
- Putin showed only a narrow procedural restraint signal in May and a broad discipline decree in March.
- The dominant 2024 pattern was **escalatory**: tactical nuclear drills, doctrine hardening, and constant-alert rhetoric tied to the Ukraine war.
- I found **no credible 2024 evidence** of a preserved deconfliction channel, a meaningful public confidence-building measure, or a durable step that materially reduced accidental-war risk.
